papers.title: DiffImp: Efficient Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation with Bidirectional Mamba Backbone
papers.methods: Denoising diffusion (DDPM) probabilistic imputer that swaps the usual Transformer denoiser for a Mamba/SSM backbone, with bidirectional and inter-variable SSM blocks for linear-time sequence modeling.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly the newest diffusion-SOTA bidirectional deep imputer CAFE positions against in its 'two-of-three' claim: it is probabilistic (uncertainty) and bidirectional (non-causal, uses full-sequence context) and GPU/deep-net heavy, so it lands in the opposite corner of CAFE's causal+CPU+competitive triangle. Mamba linear-time is its efficiency pitch vs CAFE's Cholesky-only CPU pitch.

papers.title: TIMBA: Time series Imputation with Bi-directional Mamba Blocks and Diffusion models
papers.methods: Diffusion-based imputer integrating bidirectional Mamba state-space blocks with graph neural networks and node-oriented Transformers for spatiotemporal representations.
papers.relation_to_cafe: A near-simultaneous Mamba+diffusion competitor to DiffImp; same bidirectional-deep-generative corner CAFE argues against. Notable as another 2024 entrant combining SSM with graph/transformer context, contrasting CAFE's single-pass low-rank-AR statistical core. Bidirectional => not point-in-time, the leakage CAFE's verifier targets.

papers.title: ImputeFormer: Low Rankness-Induced Transformers for Generalizable Spatiotemporal Imputation
papers.methods: Transformer with an explicit low-rank inductive bias (projected/low-rank attention) plus temporal and spatial interaction layers to balance signal and noise for spatiotemporal imputation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The closest low-rank rival to CAFE noted in its own hardening notes: it fuses CAFE's central low-rank/factor structure with deep attention. Shares the low-rank-meets-expressivity thesis but is bidirectional and learned per-dataset, whereas CAFE keeps low-rank causal, online, and dial-learned. Strong head-to-head accuracy benchmark on air-quality/traffic/solar shared datasets.

papers.title: CSAI: Conditional Self-Attention Imputation for Healthcare Time-series
papers.methods: Bidirectional RNN built on BRITS, adding transformer-based conditional self-attention hidden-state initialization, a domain-informed feature-specific temporal decay, and a non-uniform masking strategy.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Newest direct BRITS/M-RNN follow-up (the RNN lineage CAFE already cites), so it is the up-to-date version of the recurrent-imputer baseline. Its feature-specific temporal-decay is conceptually adjacent to CAFE's learned AR memory coefficient a, but it remains bidirectional and EHR-tuned rather than causal/general.

papers.title: Conditional Lagrangian Wasserstein Flow for Time Series Imputation
papers.methods: Flow-matching imputer that learns a velocity field by minimizing kinetic energy (Lagrangian mechanics) with a task-specific potential via a time-dependent denoising autoencoder, giving faster sampling than diffusion.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Represents the 2024-2025 flow-matching wave succeeding CSDI/PriSTI-style diffusion; a probabilistic generative imputer producing uncertainty like CAFE but via stochastic transport, GPU, and full-sequence conditioning (non-causal). Useful as the efficiency-oriented generative alternative to contrast with CAFE's closed-form single pass.

papers.title: ImputeINR: Time Series Imputation via Implicit Neural Representations for Disease Diagnosis with Missing Data
papers.methods: Learns continuous implicit neural representations (decoupled from sampling frequency, infinite resolution) to impute extremely sparse / high-missing-ratio time series for downstream disease diagnosis.
papers.relation_to_cafe: A 2025 continuous-modeling competitor specifically targeting the long-gap / high-missing-rate regime where CAFE reports degradation curves to 40% contiguous gap; INR's frequency-free continuous function is an alternative to CAFE's Fourier-seasonal + factor decomposition. Tests the same high-missingness stress axis.

papers.title: Are Time-Indexed Foundation Models the Future of Time Series Imputation?
papers.methods: Large-scale empirical study of zero-shot time-indexed foundation models (TabPFN-TS, MoTM) for imputation across 33 out-of-domain datasets without retraining, with inference-time covariate incorporation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The pretrained-foundation-model angle on imputation and a benchmark-style study directly relevant to CAFE's zero-config / no-per-dataset-tuning selling point: foundation models also claim no retraining, so they are the emerging rival to CAFE's 'learned-not-tuned' generality claim. Provides a fresh competitive landscape CAFE should cite to pre-empt the 'just use a TSFM' objection.

papers.title: MoTM: Towards a Foundation Model for Time Series Imputation based on Continuous Modeling
papers.methods: A foundation model for imputation built on continuous (time-indexed/INR-style) modeling, enabling zero-shot missing-value recovery across heterogeneous series.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The first explicitly imputation-dedicated foundation model, combining the continuous-modeling (INR) and pretrained-generalization threads; adjacent to CAFE as the deep-learning route to dataset-agnostic imputation without per-dataset tuning, contrasting CAFE's purely statistical online estimator.

papers.title: MOMENT: A Family of Open Time-series Foundation Models
papers.methods: Masked-patch reconstruction Transformer foundation model pretrained across many datasets, solving imputation in reconstruction mode (mask tokens for unobserved values) alongside forecasting/classification/anomaly detection.
papers.relation_to_cafe: A multi-task foundation model whose imputation-via-masked-reconstruction directly competes with CAFE's single-pass multi-output design (CAFE also yields imputation+forecast+anomaly+factors from one model). MOMENT is bidirectional and GPU-pretrained; useful contrast for CAFE's claim of one causal CPU pass delivering the same task bundle.

papers.title: Time-series imputation using low-rank matrix completion
papers.methods: Hankel Imputation (HI): low-rank nuclear-norm matrix completion applied to a block-Hankel embedding of a univariate time series, with the lag/window chosen so the Hankel matrix is approximately square.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly in CAFE's low-rank/Hankel lane: the canonical recent example of temporal low-rankness via Hankel embedding rather than CAFE's W z_t factor + AR state. Statistical (non-neural), batch, and not strictly causal (completes the whole Hankel matrix), so it is a clean comparison point CAFE can cite as the Hankel branch CAFE's AR-factor formulation supersedes online.

papers.title: ImputeFormer: Low Rankness-Induced Transformers for Generalizable Spatiotemporal Imputation
papers.methods: Transformer whose projected (low-rank) temporal/spatial attention is regularized to be low-rank, balancing low-rank inductive bias with deep expressivity at linear complexity for spatiotemporal imputation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The closest low-rank rival already flagged in CAFE notes; bidirectional deep model, GPU-leaning, not point-in-time. Include only as the low-rankness-induced-transformer follow-up CAFE explicitly contrasts (two-of-three: not causal). Likely already cited; listed for completeness of the low-rank-attention thread.

papers.title: Laplacian Convolutional Representation for Traffic Time Series Imputation
papers.methods: Unifies circulant-matrix nuclear norm (global low-rankness) with a Laplacian-kernel temporal regularizer for local smoothness, solved efficiently in closed form via FFT.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Low-rank + temporal-regularization sibling of TRMF, but with circulant/FFT machinery; a strong, recent, purely statistical low-rank imputer that CAFE should benchmark against in its 'SoftImpute/TRMF as special cases' narrative. Batch and bidirectional (not causal), so it sharpens CAFE's causal moat.

papers.title: Forecasting Sparse Movement Speed of Urban Road Networks with Nonstationary Temporal Matrix Factorization (NoTMF)
papers.venue: arXiv / journal (Chen, Zhang, Zhao, Saunier, Sun)
papers.methods: Temporal matrix factorization that imposes a higher-order VAR on a seasonally-differenced temporal factor matrix, jointly handling sparsity/missingness, nonstationarity, and seasonality.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Most structurally similar to CAFE's latent AR-on-factors core (z_t = a z_{t-1}): NoTMF puts a VAR on differenced temporal factors plus seasonal differencing, paralleling CAFE's low-rank dynamic factors + Fourier season. Key distinction: NoTMF tunes rank/orders and is not framed as strictly causal/online-empirical-Bayes, making it a direct TRMF-family competitor CAFE generalizes.

papers.title: A Parameter-free Nonconvex Low-rank Tensor Completion Model for Spatiotemporal Traffic Data Recovery (TC-PFNC / RTC-PFNC)
papers.methods: Nonconvex log-based rank surrogate for low-rank tensor completion solved by ADMM, with a robust variant (RTC-PFNC) that simultaneously handles outliers/corruption, and no rank/weight hyperparameters to tune.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Shares CAFE's 'parameter-free / learned-not-tuned' selling point and robust (heavy-tail/outlier) angle that mirrors CAFE's Student-t error. Tensor (3D) low-rank completion, batch and bidirectional; a direct competitor on the 'no per-dataset tuning' and robustness claims.

papers.title: Convolutional Low-Rank Tensor Representation for Structural Missing Traffic Data Imputation (CLRTR)
papers.methods: Convolutional low-rank tensor representation that targets structured missingness (tube-/slice-missing from sensor outages) rather than random MCAR, capturing local convolutional structure plus global low-rankness.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Adjacent on the tensor low-rank front but specializes in block/structured missing patterns, overlapping CAFE's point/subsequence/block 10/30/50% stratification. Useful as a recent low-rank baseline emphasizing structural (non-MCAR) gaps; not causal/online.

papers.title: A Spatio-Temporal Online Robust Tensor Recovery Approach for Streaming Traffic Data Imputation
papers.methods: Online (streaming) robust low-rank tensor recovery that jointly imputes missing values and removes anomalies using global spatio-temporal correlation plus local consistency, ~1000x faster than batch tensor completion.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The most directly threatening: it is ONLINE + low-rank + robust + does anomaly handling, hitting three things CAFE claims (causal/streaming, robustness, anomaly score) within a low-rank framework. CAFE should differentiate on strict point-in-time truncation-invariance, per-cell uncertainty, and learned dials vs this method's tuned regularizers; clear comparison/competitor.

papers.title: A Survey and Benchmarking of Spatial-Temporal Traffic Data Imputation Models
papers.methods: Survey + unified empirical benchmark of spatiotemporal imputation models (low-rank tensor/matrix completion methods alongside deep/graph methods) across missingness patterns and datasets.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Benchmark/landscape paper that situates low-rank completion vs deep imputers under common protocols, directly relevant to CAFE's 'mismatched registries / no single leaderboard' caveat and its benchmark() positioning; a citation for the competitive landscape and for hardening CAFE against TSI-Bench-style critiques.

papers.title: Low-Rank Autoregressive Tensor Completion for Spatiotemporal Traffic Data Imputation (LATC)
papers.methods: Folds a multivariate series into a third-order (sensor x time-of-day x day) tensor and adds an autoregressive temporal-variation regularizer to truncated-nuclear-norm tensor completion.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The tensor-completion ancestor that, like CAFE, couples low-rankness with an explicit autoregressive temporal model; CAFE's z_t=a z_{t-1} factor dynamics are the matrix/online analogue. Strong 'special case / predecessor' citation showing CAFE unifies AR + low-rank without per-dataset rank/AR tuning and without look-ahead.

papers.title: Estimation of Large Approximate Dynamic Matrix Factor Models Based on the EM Algorithm and Kalman Filtering
papers.methods: Quasi-maximum-likelihood estimation of large approximate dynamic matrix factor models via EM jointly with the Kalman smoother, explicitly modeling factor dynamics and handling arbitrary missing-data patterns and common stochastic trends.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly comparable factor/state-space core: this is the econometrics-side analogue of CAFE's Kalman/SSM dynamic-factor regime (z_t = a z_{t-1} + noise) fit by EM, but it is offline/full-sample (smoother, not strictly causal) and has no learned tails/season/uncertainty-per-cell; the most threatening 'large approximate dynamic factor model' reference.

papers.title: Tensor Time Series Imputation through Tensor Factor Modelling
papers.methods: Tensor factor model with Tucker decomposition of the common component, allowing weak factors per mode, with a ratio-based core-rank estimator and asymptotic normality of loadings under general missing patterns; imputes via the estimated common component.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Low-rank factor imputation extended to 3D/tensor panels with formal asymptotic inference — adjacent on the factor/low-rank and panel axes, and relevant to CAFE's 3D claim; offline and inference-focused rather than online/causal, no uncertainty cones or learned dials.

papers.title: Large Dimensional Latent Factor Modeling with Missing Observations and Applications to Causal Inference
papers.methods: Applies PCA to an adjusted covariance matrix estimated from partially observed panels, deriving the asymptotic distribution of estimated factors, loadings, and imputed values under approximate factor models with general missing patterns; used for counterfactual/causal estimation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Factor-based imputation with explicit per-imputed-value inference and a causal/counterfactual framing — overlaps CAFE on factor structure, panel missingness, AND the causal-inference angle, but causal here means treatment-effect counterfactuals (not point-in-time/no-leakage) and the estimator is full-sample.

papers.title: Factor-Based Imputation of Missing Values and Covariances in Panel Data of Large Dimensions
papers.methods: TALL-PROJECT algorithm: estimate factors from a fully observed TALL block, project to get loadings, impute missing entries by their estimated common component; consistent and asymptotically normal without iteration, also imputes covariances.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Canonical large-dimensional approximate-factor imputation baseline (Bai-Ng line); a special-case-style competitor to CAFE's low-rank component, but block-structured/offline and lacking dynamics, tails, season, and online operation.

papers.title: Streaming Heteroscedastic Probabilistic PCA with Missing Data (SHASTA-PCA)
papers.methods: Stochastic alternating EM that jointly learns low-rank latent factors and per-variable heteroscedastic noise variances from streaming data with missing entries, at low memory/compute.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Closest 'streaming PCA for incomplete data' rival: online, probabilistic, missing-data, and it learns noise variances by EM much like CAFE learns its dials by empirical Bayes; differs in being Gaussian/heteroscedastic (no Student-t tails, AR dynamics, season, or causal-leakage verification).

papers.title: Provable Subspace Tracking from Missing Data and Matrix Completion (NORST-miss)
papers.methods: Alternates projected least-squares (fill missing entries) and subspace update on mini-batches to provably track a piecewise-constant low-rank subspace from missing/corrupted data; doubles as memory-efficient online matrix completion.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Foundational provable subspace-tracking-with-missing-data method (the GROUSE/PETRELS lineage CAFE's online low-rank component competes with); strictly streaming with guarantees but no probabilistic uncertainty, no fixed effects/season, and assumes piecewise-constant rather than AR-driven factors.

papers.title: A Spatio-Temporal Online Robust Tensor Recovery Approach for Streaming Traffic Data Imputation
papers.methods: Online robust low-rank tensor recovery that incrementally updates factors as new slices stream in, exploiting spatio-temporal structure and outlier-robustness for large-scale sensor streams with lower memory than batch methods.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Very recent online + low-rank + robust streaming imputer on the same kind of spatiotemporal sensor panels CAFE targets; robustness here is outlier separation rather than Student-t likelihood, and it is tensor/batch-incremental rather than per-cell causal with uncertainty.

papers.title: BayOTIDE: Bayesian Online Multivariate Time Series Imputation with Functional Decomposition
papers.methods: First online probabilistic imputer for multivariate time series: weighted combination of low-rank temporal factors with distinct patterns, inferred via a scalable online GP-SDE bridge that yields per-timestamp uncertainty and handles irregular/arbitrary timestamps.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The single most directly comparable method and a head-to-head competitor: online + low-rank factor decomposition + uncertainty quantification + interpretable level/trend/factor decomposition. Differs from CAFE in being Bayesian-GP rather than a unified penalised EM with learned Student-t tails and AR memory; CAFE should benchmark against it as the leading causal/online rival.

papers.title: Streaming Heteroscedastic Probabilistic PCA with Missing Data (SHASTA-PCA)
papers.methods: Streaming/online probabilistic PCA that jointly learns low-rank latent factors and per-sample (heteroscedastic) noise variances from incomplete data via stochastic alternating EM with low memory footprint.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Methodologically very close to CAFE's core: online low-rank factor estimation under missingness with adaptive, non-uniform noise (heteroscedasticity parallels CAFE's learned Student-t scale). A natural baseline for the streaming low-rank + robust-noise niche; lacks CAFE's seasonality, AR factor dynamics, and panel fixed effects.

papers.title: Assessing Look-Ahead Bias in Stock Return Predictions Generated by GPT Sentiment Analysis
papers.methods: Isolates look-ahead bias vs a 'distraction effect' in LLM news-sentiment trading signals by comparing original against anonymized headlines, using in-sample/out-of-sample tests to debias backtests.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Canonical look-ahead-bias-in-finance reference directly supporting CAFE's causal/point-in-time motivation and its reported-vs-live walk-forward argument; complementary (LLM/finance framing, not an imputer). Strong citation to anchor the leakage narrative.

papers.title: Standardized Benchmark of Look-ahead Bias in Point-in-Time Financial LLMs (LookAheadBench)
papers.methods: An evaluation framework (LookAheadBench) using a dual-period train/eval separation and trading baselines (buy-and-hold, momentum, mean-reversion) to quantify temporal information leakage and test point-in-time data implementations.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Benchmark/leakage-quantification adjacency: formalizes a standardized point-in-time look-ahead-bias protocol, the exact contamination CAFE's truncation-invariance verifier defends against. Reinforces CAFE's claim that the causal/PIT niche is unoccupied and offers a comparison protocol; finance-LLM focused rather than imputation.

papers.title: Hidden Leaks in Time Series Forecasting: How Data Leakage Affects LSTM Evaluation Across Configurations and Validation Strategies
papers.methods: Empirically quantifies data leakage from pre-split sequence construction in LSTM forecasting via an 'RMSE Gain' metric (leaky vs clean), showing k-fold CV inflates accuracy up to ~20% while strict temporal splits stay under 5%.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly supports CAFE's leakage/look-ahead thesis with a concrete measurement of how non-causal evaluation inflates deep-model scores, mirroring CAFE's 'right-edge readout collapse' horse race. Methodology adjacency: leakage diagnostics rather than a new imputer.

papers.title: Causal View of Time Series Imputation: Some Identification Results on Missing Mechanism (DMM)
papers.methods: Models MAR/MNAR generation with temporal latent states and missing-cause variables, estimated by variational inference with normalizing flows, and proves latent-variable identifiability via nonlinear ICA.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Direct adjacency on the MNAR/missing-mechanism and recoverability axis that CAFE cites for its honest non-identifiability scope note (the Ma & Zhang causal-view lever). Provides the formal causal-identification counterpart to CAFE's pragmatic stance; 'causal' here is structural-mechanism, not strict point-in-time.

papers.title: Causality-Aware Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Spatiotemporal Time Series Imputation (Casper)
papers.methods: Uses frontdoor adjustment to block confounders, with a prompt-based decoder and a Spatiotemporal Causal Attention module that discovers sparse causal dependencies among sensor-node embeddings for imputation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Shares the 'causal' branding and the cross-sectional dependency-network angle (sparse inter-node causal graph parallels CAFE's dependency network), but is offline/bidirectional and uses structural (backdoor) causality, not temporal point-in-time causality. Useful contrast to sharpen CAFE's distinct causal-direction claim.

papers.title: Online Missing Value Imputation and Change Point Detection with the Gaussian Copula
papers.methods: Online Gaussian-copula imputation for mixed-type streaming data that updates incrementally, adapts to distribution shift, detects change points in the dependence structure, and is ~10x faster than its offline counterpart.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Closest pre-deep-learning online/streaming imputation baseline with built-in change/anomaly detection on the correlation structure, mirroring CAFE's streaming anomaly score and online dependency network. A newer online follow-up to the copula line CAFE already cites; non-causal-deep, CPU-friendly, no seasonality/AR factors.

papers.title: Robust Matrix Completion with Heavy-Tailed Noise
papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, Vol 120 No 550 (arXiv 2022)
papers.methods: Adaptive Huber loss combined with a balanced Burer-Monteiro low-rank factorization and gradient descent with robust spectral initialization, achieving minimax-optimal error under only a bounded second-moment noise condition.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly the robust/heavy-tailed matrix-completion line CAFE positions against: it makes outlier-robustness the central object via Huber loss rather than CAFE's Student-t(nu) likelihood, and is low-rank but batch/offline (not causal, not online, no factor dynamics or uncertainty). The canonical heavy-tailed MC reference to cite for the robustness facet.

papers.title: T-Rex: Fitting a Robust Factor Model via Expectation-Maximization
papers.methods: EM algorithm fitting a low-rank-plus-diagonal statistical factor model under an elliptical distribution using Tyler's M-estimator of scatter, robust to heavy tails and outliers.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Very close methodological sibling: a robust low-rank factor model fit by EM under a heavy-tailed (elliptical) likelihood, exactly CAFE's W z_t + Student-t structure but estimated via Tyler M-estimation instead of empirical-Bayes Student-t. Lacks CAFE's causal/online pass, AR factor dynamics, seasonality, and imputation focus, making it the most directly comparable robust-factor estimator.

papers.title: Tail-robust factor modelling of vector and tensor time series in high dimensions
papers.methods: Two-step tensor/vector factor decomposition combined with data truncation to handle heavy tails, with consistency and asymptotic normality under only a (2+2e)-th moment condition and a factor-number criterion.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Robust factor modelling for high-dimensional time series and panels (applied to macro data like FRED-MD), the same statistical-factor regime CAFE operates in but addressing heavy tails by truncation rather than a Student-t likelihood; non-causal and not imputation-oriented. Strong adjacent factor-model competitor.

papers.title: A Spatio-Temporal Online Robust Tensor Recovery Approach for Streaming Traffic Data Imputation
papers.methods: Online robust low-rank tensor recovery that exploits global spatio-temporal correlation and local consistency to simultaneously impute missing values and remove anomalies in streaming traffic data, up to 3 orders of magnitude faster than batch methods.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The most directly competitive in spirit: online/streaming, robust to outliers, joint imputation + anomaly handling, low-rank, fast on large panels, on traffic data CAFE also uses. Differs in being a tensor RPCA-style decomposition (no explicit causal truncation guarantee, factor/AR dynamics, or calibrated per-cell uncertainty). Closest 'online robust imputation' rival.

papers.title: Robust PCA Based on Adaptive Weighted Least Squares and Low-Rank Matrix Factorization
papers.methods: RPCA decomposing data into low-rank plus sparse components using adaptive weighted least squares (a self-attention-inspired reweighting that acts like IRLS) over a low-rank matrix factorization, solved by alternating minimization with closed-form subproblems.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Embodies the iteratively-reweighted-least-squares-for-low-rank facet: adaptive per-residual weighting plus low-rank factorization is exactly the IRLS mechanism CAFE's Student-t EM induces (downweighting outliers). Batch RPCA, no temporal/causal structure, so it anchors the IRLS-RPCA comparison rather than competing on imputation.

papers.title: Robust Low-Rank Matrix Completion via a New Sparsity-Inducing Regularizer
papers.methods: Introduces a hybrid ordinary-Welsch (HOW) loss and an associated quasiconvex sparsity-inducing regularizer with closed-form proximity operator, applied to robust matrix completion via ADMM.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Robust (outlier-resistant) low-rank matrix completion using a redescending M-estimator-style loss, an alternative to CAFE's Student-t for downweighting gross errors. Offline, no time/factor dynamics or uncertainty; representative of the recent robust-MC regularizer literature CAFE should distinguish from.

papers.title: The Spurious Factor Dilemma: Robust Inference in Heavy-Tailed Elliptical Factor Models
papers.methods: A fluctuation-magnification testing procedure that determines the number of common factors in heavy-tailed elliptical factor models by exploiting that true-factor eigenvalues fluctuate less than spurious heavy-tail-induced eigenvalues.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Targets robust rank/factor-number selection under heavy tails, the same elliptical heavy-tailed factor regime CAFE assumes, and directly relevant to CAFE's learned ARD effective-rank claim (heavy tails can inflate apparent rank). Inference/selection focus, not imputation.

papers.title: Robust reduced rank regression under heavy-tailed noise and missing data via non-convex penalization
papers.methods: Robust reduced-rank regression combining a Huber loss with nonconvex spectral penalties (MCP/SCAD) to handle heavy-tailed noise, outliers, and missing data, solved by a proximal gradient algorithm with closed-form proximal maps.
papers.relation_to_cafe: One of the few recent works jointly handling heavy-tailed noise AND missing data in a low-rank model, the exact intersection CAFE occupies, but via Huber + nonconvex rank penalty in a regression (not online time-series imputation) setting with no causal/streaming or uncertainty component. Adjacent robust-low-rank-with-missingness competitor.

papers.title: Counterfactual Forecasting for Panel Data (FOCUS: Forecasting Counterfactuals under Stochastic Dynamics)
papers.methods: Extends low-rank matrix completion for panels by layering stationary autoregressive (AR) dynamics on the latent factors so that unobserved potential outcomes can be forecast ahead of time, not just imputed in-sample.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The single most directly comparable/threatening prior work: it combines the SAME two structural ingredients as CAFE's core (low-rank dynamic factors + AR latent state z_t=a z_{t-1}) to do causal counterfactual forecasting on panels with missing entries. Differs from CAFE in lacking fixed effects, Fourier season, Student-t robustness, learned dials, per-cell uncertainty, and CAFE's truncation-invariance causal verifier, but it occupies CAFE's exact 'factor + temporal dynamics + forecasting' niche and must be cited/contrasted.

papers.title: Matrix Completion When Missing Is Not at Random and Its Applications in Causal Panel Data Models
papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA)
papers.methods: Develops an inferential framework for nuclear-norm matrix completion under MNAR (e.g. selection into treatment), showing entries are recoverable without strong-signal assumptions when the treated/missing fraction is small relative to panel size.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly targets CAFE's admitted open item that MNAR bias is not explicitly modelled; gives a recoverability/identification lever for non-random missingness in causal panel matrix completion (the MC-NNM lineage CAFE claims as a special case). A natural citation for CAFE's MNAR scope note and a benchmark for the MNAR-robustness claim.

papers.title: Estimating Counterfactual Matrix Means with Short Panel Data
papers.methods: A spectral (factor-model) approach to identify and estimate average counterfactual outcomes under a low-rank factor model with short (fixed-T, large-N) panels and general missingness, positioned as a more flexible alternative to two-way fixed effects.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Adjacent low-rank-factor + fixed-effects-replacement method for causal panels; relevant to CAFE's 'TWFE/MC-NNM are special cases' framing and its fixed-effect absorption design. Contrasts with CAFE by being fixed-T/large-N and non-causal-in-time (no point-in-time constraint), highlighting CAFE's causal/online distinction.

papers.title: Inference for Low-rank Completion without Sample Splitting with Application to Treatment Effect Estimation
papers.methods: Least-squares re-estimation of eigenvectors after nuclear-norm penalization yields asymptotically normal low-rank matrix estimates without sample splitting, applied to panel treatment-effect estimation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Provides the inferential/uncertainty theory layer for the MC-NNM low-rank panel completion family that CAFE subsumes; relevant to CAFE's per-cell uncertainty and calibration discussion (CAFE admits intervals are over-conservative). A reference point for how the econometrics side does valid inference on low-rank completions.

papers.title: Data-driven Model Selection within the Matrix Completion Method for Causal Panel Data Models
papers.methods: Uses nuclear-norm minimization to automatically regularize factor-model rank while jointly regularizing high-dimensional covariates, with permutation-based inference valid under any treatment assignment.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly addresses automatic rank/model selection in MC-NNM causal panel completion, which parallels CAFE's learned (not tuned) ARD effective rank and its 'no per-dataset tuning / no model selection' selling point. A close competitor on the 'data-driven, not hand-tuned' axis within the matrix-completion-for-panels literature.

papers.title: Inferring Treatment Effects in Large Panels by Uncovering Latent Similarities
papers.methods: Imputes untreated potential outcomes for treated units by matching on estimated latent confounders under a nonparametric nonlinear nonseparable factor model, yielding a doubly-robust period-specific ATT estimator.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Adjacent nearest-neighbor/latent-factor counterfactual-imputation approach for large panels (large N,T); represents the nonlinear/nonparametric factor alternative to CAFE's linear-Gaussian-factor core. Useful contrast for CAFE's claim that a single linear penalised model suffices, and for the panel imputation-for-causal-inference framing.

papers.title: Large Dimensional Latent Factor Modeling with Missing Observations and Applications to Causal Inference
papers.methods: Factor-based (PCA/projected-PCA) imputation of a large time-series panel with pervasive factors under very general missingness patterns, with asymptotic normality and inference for the imputed values.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Canonical recent econometric factor-imputation method that is the direct ancestor/competitor to CAFE's low-rank-factor imputation on macro/financial panels (FRED-MD-style); establishes the interactive-fixed-effects + missing-data lineage CAFE situates itself within. A newer follow-up beyond the older Bai-Ng citations, valuable for the panel-econometrics positioning.

papers.title: Robust Matrix Completion with Heavy-Tailed Noise
papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association (JASA)
papers.methods: Noisy low-rank matrix completion under heavy-tailed/asymmetric noise via an adaptive Huber loss with Burer-Monteiro factorization and robust spectral initialization, achieving minimax-optimal error under only a bounded-second-moment assumption.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The heavy-tailed-robust complement to the low-rank matrix completion family CAFE generalizes; directly relevant to CAFE's Student-t(nu) error / excess-kurtosis robustness dial. Shows the matrix-completion community's answer (Huber) to the same heavy-tail problem CAFE solves with learned Student-t degrees of freedom, making it a methodological sibling worth contrasting.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction with Missing Values
papers.methods: Adapts split-conformal / conformalized quantile regression to settings where covariates are missing, proving marginal coverage holds on imputed data for any missingness distribution and introducing a 'missing data augmentation' that makes intervals valid conditional on the (exponentially many) missing patterns.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Conformal + missing data + calibration of predictive intervals; directly addresses CAFE's admitted open item (intervals over-conservative / not pattern-conditionally calibrated). Distribution-free coverage is the rigorous alternative to CAFE's PICP/PIT reliability story and a natural recalibration wrapper to cite.

papers.title: Conformalized Matrix Completion
papers.methods: Wraps any low-rank matrix-completion algorithm in a conformal procedure to produce distribution-free predictive intervals for missing entries that retain coverage regardless of low-rank model misspecification, with weighting to handle non-uniform sampling.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Low-rank + uncertainty + distribution-free calibration on exactly CAFE's panel/matrix imputation setting; the canonical 'rigorous coverage for low-rank imputation' baseline CAFE's conservative ADMITS intervals should be benchmarked against. Shares CAFE's low-rank factor lineage but offers guarantees CAFE currently lacks.

papers.title: Deep sub-ensembles meets quantile regression: uncertainty-aware imputation for time series (Quantile Sub-Ensembles)
papers.methods: Non-generative imputer that estimates per-cell uncertainty via ensembles of quantile-regression task networks (deep sub-ensembles), targeting both deterministic accuracy and probabilistic calibration at lower cost than diffusion.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Most directly competitive on CAFE's exact pitch: cheaper, non-generative, uncertainty-aware time-series imputation evaluated on probabilistic metrics. A rival 'accuracy + calibrated uncertainty without a heavy generative model' claim; strong head-to-head comparison and a recalibration idea (quantile ensembling) CAFE could borrow.

papers.title: Latent Space Score-based Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Multivariate Time Series Imputation (LSSDM)
papers.methods: Two-stage probabilistic imputer that projects observations to a low-dimensional latent space, reconstructs coarse missing values by unsupervised learning, then refines via a conditional score-based diffusion model, yielding samples and uncertainty.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Newer CSDI-family follow-up (CSDI itself already cited) combining low-rank/latent compression with diffusion for probabilistic imputation; a current deep-generative SOTA contender on CAFE's CRPS/coverage axis and a bidirectional rival for the causal horse race.

papers.title: DiffImp: Efficient Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation with Bidirectional Mamba Backbone
papers.methods: Conditional diffusion imputer replacing transformer attention with a bidirectional Mamba (state-space) backbone for efficiency, evaluated with CRPS / CRPS-sum on standard multivariate benchmarks.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Probabilistic diffusion imputation scored on CRPS (CAFE's headline uncertainty metric) and explicitly chasing efficiency; an efficiency-aware deep-generative competitor to CAFE's CPU-only probabilistic claim, and a fresh SAITS/CSDI-era baseline.

papers.title: Weighted Conformal Prediction Provides Adaptive and Valid Mask-Conditional Coverage for General Missing Data Mechanisms
papers.methods: A preimpute-mask-then-correct framework that reweights conformity scores via multiple imputation to deliver both marginal and mask-conditional coverage under general (incl. MNAR-leaning) missingness, producing narrower valid intervals.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Conformal + multiple imputation + missingness-mechanism-robust calibration; engages CAFE's MNAR/non-identifiability and conservative-interval open items simultaneously. Mask-conditional validity is a sharper calibration target than CAFE's marginal PICP and a citable route to fix it.

papers.title: Diffusion Transformers for Imputation: Statistical Efficiency and Uncertainty Quantification
papers.methods: Provides approximation/sample-complexity theory for conditional score functions realized by diffusion transformers and uses the bounds to construct tight confidence regions for imputed values, analyzing how missing patterns affect statistical efficiency.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Rare theoretical treatment of uncertainty quantification and statistical efficiency for generative imputation, tying calibration to missing-pattern structure; complements CAFE's empirical reliability diagrams with the kind of statistical-rigor framing CAFE markets, and is a forward-looking competitor's UQ benchmark.

papers.title: Leveraging Variational Autoencoders for Multiple Data Imputation
papers.methods: Uses importance-weighted / multiple-imputation VAEs to draw several plausible completions per missing cell and studies whether the resulting posterior predictive properly propagates imputation uncertainty (NLL grows with missingness), highlighting under-/over-confidence.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Deep generative multiple imputation with explicit uncertainty-propagation diagnostics; the Bayesian/multiple-imputation reference point for CAFE's per-cell uncertainty, and a documented case of mis-calibration under high missingness that motivates CAFE's calibration discussion. Slightly older but the cleanest MI-VAE anchor; pair with the conformal entries for a calibration-vs-Bayesian contrast.

papers.title: TSI-Bench: Benchmarking Time Series Imputation
papers.methods: A unified benchmark of 28 imputation/forecasting-based time-series algorithms over 8 datasets in 4 domains, standardizing experimental settings and systematically injecting MCAR/MAR/MNAR missingness at varied rates/patterns across 34,804 experiments.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The central benchmark/evaluation-protocol paper CAFE explicitly engages with (the 'TSI-Bench vs SAITS registry disagreement' caveat); directly defines the MCAR/MAR/MNAR + pattern/rate protocol CAFE must be measured against. Highest adjacency as the benchmark CAFE positions itself within.

papers.title: Benchmarking Missing Data Imputation Methods for Time Series Using Real-World Test Cases
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 6th Conference on Health, Inference, and Learning (CHIL), PMLR vol. 287
papers.methods: Benchmarks 12 time-series imputers under MCAR/MAR/NMAR and across demographic subgroups using real-world clinical data, contrasting randomly-deleted-value evaluation against realistic missingness.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Benchmark + evaluation-pitfalls paper; finds simple linear interpolation beats 11 SOTA methods across all mechanisms, and that MCAR-style evaluation overstates real-world accuracy — directly supports CAFE's 'deep SOTA edge evaporates / LOCF can win on smooth series' and MNAR-honesty narrative.

papers.title: Imputation for prediction: beware of diminishing returns
papers.methods: Large empirical/theoretical study showing that, with expressive predictive models plus missingness indicators, improving imputation quality yields only minor downstream prediction gains.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Evaluation-protocol / downstream-utility critique adjacent to CAFE's XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost downstream-task experiments and its reported-vs-live walk-forward argument; tempers claims that better reconstruction = better downstream, a pitfall CAFE's benchmarking section navigates.

papers.title: Do we Need Dozens of Methods for Real World Missing Value Imputation?
papers.methods: Benchmarks ~73 imputation algorithms across 24 datasets under artificial and real missingness, evaluating distributional fidelity (not just RMSE) and finding classical FCS/mice methods consistently match or beat deep learning.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Experimental-survey / benchmark-pitfalls paper supporting CAFE's 'two-of-three' thesis that simple causal/statistical methods rival deep SOTA; uses distributional rather than pure-error metrics, relevant to CAFE's CRPS/PICP uncertainty evaluation framing.

papers.title: Task-oriented Time Series Imputation Evaluation via Generalized Representers
papers.methods: Evaluates time-series imputation by estimating downstream-task gain without retraining (via generalized representers), then composes imputations to maximize that task-specific gain.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Evaluation-protocol paper arguing reconstruction error is the wrong objective and downstream task value should drive imputation choice — directly adjacent to CAFE's downstream-utility experiments and its critique of reconstruction-only leaderboards.

papers.title: Deep Generative Imputation Model for Missing Not At Random Data (GNR)
papers.methods: A deep generative model treating complete data and the missing mask as two equal modalities, jointly imputing values and reconstructing the missingness pattern in latent space to handle MNAR.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly addresses the MNAR-bias modelling gap CAFE openly admits it does not model; a recent, competitive not-missing-at-random method and natural point of comparison/citation for CAFE's MNAR scope note.

papers.title: An Interdisciplinary and Cross-Task Review on Missing Data Imputation
papers.methods: A broad cross-disciplinary survey of imputation covering classical, deep, generative and LLM-based methods, missingness mechanisms, specialized data formats, and integration with downstream tasks.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Recent experimental/methodological survey of imputation that situates CAFE among classical-vs-deep and causal/mechanism-aware approaches; useful related-work anchor distinct from the deep-MTS-only surveys CAFE likely already cites.

papers.title: IMAGIC-500: IMputation benchmark on A Generative Imaginary Country (500k samples)
papers.methods: A 500k-sample synthetic socioeconomic benchmark with a known generative ground truth, evaluating classical, ML and deep imputers across feature types and controlled MCAR/MAR/MNAR mechanisms.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Tabular/panel benchmarking-protocol paper with controlled missingness mechanisms and large-scale fair comparison — adjacent to CAFE's structured-panel datasets and its published-number-registry/no-single-leaderboard caveat.

papers.title: Diffusion-based Time Series Imputation and Forecasting with Structured State Space Models (SSSD / SSSD^S4)
papers.methods: Conditional denoising diffusion model with a structured state-space (S4) backbone to capture long-range temporal dependencies, jointly handling imputation and forecasting under varied missingness (random, block, blackout).
papers.relation_to_cafe: Seminal deep state-space imputer and the canonical S4/SSM target CAFE positions against; bidirectional deep generative SOTA (NOT causal, GPU-leaning) — directly exercises CAFE's two-of-three claim. CAFE cites CSDI but this S4 successor is the SSM-specific competitor.

papers.title: Neural Continuous-Discrete State Space Models for Irregularly-Sampled Time Series (NCDSSM)
papers.methods: Deep continuous-discrete SSM with auxiliary variables disentangling recognition from dynamics; uses continuous-discrete (Kalman-type) Bayesian filtering/smoothing for accurate latent-state inference and marginalization, giving probabilistic imputation/forecasting on irregular and missing data.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Most methodologically adjacent on the Kalman/state-space + uncertainty axis: explicit Bayesian filter/smoother latent-state inference with UQ, the deep-learning analogue of CAFE's z_t = a z_{t-1} dynamic-factor recursion. Probabilistic and handles missingness, but neural and amortized rather than closed-form causal.

papers.title: Mining of Switching Sparse Networks for Missing Value Imputation in Multivariate Time Series (MissNet)
papers.methods: State-space model for temporal dependency combined with switching sparse (conditional-independence) networks that change over time, yielding interpretable inter-variable structure plus imputation with linear scalability.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly competitive: a CPU-friendly, interpretable state-space imputer that also recovers a cross-sectional dependency network — overlapping with CAFE's dependency-network and decomposition outputs. The EM/SSM MISSNET lineage CAFE explicitly redesigned away from for speed; closest classical-SSM rival on the same panels.

papers.title: SSD-TS: Exploring the Potential of Linear State Space Models for Diffusion Models in Time Series Imputation
papers.methods: Uses Mamba (linear/selective SSM) as a custom denoising backbone inside a diffusion probabilistic model for time-series imputation, designing SSM blocks tailored to temporal dependencies.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Low-rank/linear-SSM + diffusion competitor on the same imputation benchmarks; tests whether linear SSM efficiency (a CAFE selling point) can rival attention backbones. Bidirectional/generative, not causal — fits the two-of-three contrast.

papers.title: TIMBA: Time Series Imputation with Bi-directional Mamba Blocks and Diffusion Models
papers.methods: Replaces Transformers with bidirectional Mamba (S6) state-space blocks combined with graph neural networks and node-oriented Transformers inside a diffusion model for spatiotemporal multivariate imputation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Recent Mamba-based deep SSM imputer reporting SOTA across missingness patterns; representative bidirectional deep-SSM rival on the accuracy axis that CAFE must beat causally. Explicitly bidirectional (look-ahead) — clean foil for CAFE's right-edge-readout collapse experiment.

papers.title: S4M: S4 for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Missing Values
papers.methods: End-to-end S4 framework integrating missingness directly into the model via an Adaptive Temporal Prototype Mapper and a Missing-Aware Dual-Stream S4, avoiding separate impute-then-forecast pipelines.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Joint imputation-aware forecasting with a structured-SSM core, mirroring CAFE's single-pass impute+forecast design; strong on high missing ratios. Deep S4 rather than closed-form causal factor model, so a direct architecture-level comparison point.

papers.title: KalMamba: Towards Efficient Probabilistic State Space Models for RL under Uncertainty
papers.methods: Uses Mamba to learn the parameters of a latent linear-Gaussian SSM, then performs exact Kalman filtering and smoothing in that latent space with a parallelized implementation for scalable probabilistic inference.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Tightest conceptual match to CAFE's mechanism: a learned linear-Gaussian state-space with closed-form Kalman filter/smoother and principled uncertainty, scaled efficiently. Domain is RL not imputation, but the filtering+UQ+efficiency triad is exactly CAFE's statistical engine in neural clothing.

papers.title: Temporal Gaussian Copula for Clinical Multivariate Time Series Data Imputation (TGC)
papers.methods: Gaussian-copula model capturing cross-variable and cross-time dependence, fit by an Expectation-Maximization algorithm, for robust imputation of irregularly missing multivariate (clinical) series.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Newer follow-up to the Gaussian-copula baseline CAFE already cites: adds explicit temporal coupling and EM fitting, paralleling CAFE's EM/empirical-Bayes estimation and Student-t-style robustness. CPU-friendly statistical (non-neural) imputer — a direct same-family competitor distinct from the static copula CAFE references.

papers.title: Missing Financial Data
papers.methods: Bryzgalova, Lerner, Lettau, Pelger impute the panel of firm fundamentals via a cross-sectional latent factor (per-month PCA) model exploiting both cross-sectional and time-series dependence, with explicit backward (B-XS, past-only) versus backward-forward (BF-XS) variants to handle look-ahead.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The canonical financial-panel firm-characteristics imputation reference and a direct factor-model competitor; their B-XS/BF-XS split is exactly CAFE's causal-vs-bidirectional distinction, and their PCA factor model is a regime CAFE claims to subsume (low-rank cross-sectional factors). Most directly comparable on the finance side.

papers.title: Missing Values Handling for Machine Learning Portfolios
papers.methods: Chen & McCoy characterize missingness structure across 159 cross-sectional return predictors and show that simple cross-sectional mean imputation is competitive with rigorous EM/factor methods for downstream ML portfolio performance, since sophisticated imputation injects estimation noise.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Downstream-aware finance result: argues better imputation does not buy better portfolios and warns of look-ahead leakage in global imputation — both central CAFE themes (downstream utility table, reported-vs-live walk-forward). A skeptical baseline CAFE must beat or contextualize.

papers.title: ACT-Tensor: Tensor Completion Framework for Financial Dataset Imputation (Tensor-Empowered Asset Pricing with Missing Data)
papers.methods: Cluster-based CP/HOSVD tensor completion over the firm x time x variable panel with a temporal smoothing module (CMA/EMA/Kalman), evaluated on imputation accuracy and downstream asset-pricing/portfolio returns under extreme sparsity.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Newest direct competitor to Bryzgalova/Pelger on financial-panel imputation; 3D (tensor/panel) low-rank + temporal smoothing overlaps CAFE's low-rank-plus-AR panel engine, and it is explicitly backtest/asset-pricing-evaluated. Strong factor/low-rank rival in the finance niche.

papers.title: Bayesian Imputation with Optimal Look-Ahead-Bias and Variance Tradeoff (and Wasserstein-interpolation variant)
papers.methods: Formalizes the look-ahead-bias vs variance tradeoff in imputing missing asset returns before downstream portfolio optimization, proposing a Bayesian (and Wasserstein-interpolation) imputer that interpolates between past-only and full-sample imputation.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Directly about backtesting/look-ahead leakage from imputation in finance — the exact phenomenon CAFE's truncation-invariance verifier and reported-vs-live experiment target. Frames leakage as a tunable tradeoff rather than CAFE's strict point-in-time guarantee.

papers.title: Task-oriented Time Series Imputation Evaluation via Generalized Representers
papers.methods: Estimates the gain of different imputation strategies on a downstream task using generalized representer theorems, avoiding costly retraining, to select imputations by downstream value rather than reconstruction error.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Core downstream-aware/task-oriented imputation reference: argues imputation should be judged by downstream task performance, paralleling CAFE's downstream-utility (XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost) evaluation. Adjacent methodology for the 'does imputation accuracy matter' axis.

papers.title: Is Precise Recovery Necessary? A Task-Oriented Imputation Approach for Time Series Forecasting on Variable Subset (TOI-VSF)
papers.methods: Self-supervised, forecasting-model-agnostic imputation module trained by masked reconstruction but regularized by the downstream forecasting loss, targeting variable-subset forecasting where whole variables are missing.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Explicitly task-oriented: shifts objective from accurate recovery to downstream forecasting utility, directly on-topic for imputation-effect-on-forecasting. Contrasts with CAFE's single unsupervised generative objective that yields forecasting as a byproduct.

papers.title: Imputation for Prediction: Beware of Diminishing Returns
papers.methods: Large empirical study (Le Morvan & Varoquaux) showing imputation accuracy matters less with expressive models and missingness indicators, that constant imputation is often competitive, and that the imputation->prediction link is weak on real outcomes.
papers.relation_to_cafe: Sharpens the downstream-aware narrative: better imputation does not reliably improve downstream tasks — exactly the caveat CAFE must answer in its downstream-utility section. Adjacent evidence base on the imputation-quality-propagation question.

papers.title: Causality-Aware Spatiotemporal Graph Neural Networks for Spatiotemporal Time Series Imputation (Casper)
papers.methods: Spatiotemporal GNN imputer using frontdoor adjustment to block confounders, with a prompt-based decoder and a sparse spatiotemporal causal attention that discovers causal (rather than merely correlational) edges among sensor embeddings.
papers.relation_to_cafe: A 'causal' GNN follow-up in the GRIN/SPIN spatiotemporal lineage; uses 'causal' in the structural/confounder sense versus CAFE's point-in-time/no-look-ahead sense — a useful contrast on what 'causal imputation' means, and a deep bidirectional competitor.

papers.title: Learning to Reconstruct Missing Data from Spatiotemporal Graphs with Sparse Observations (SPIN)
papers.methods: Sparse spatiotemporal attention GNN (Marisca, Cini, Alippi) that imputes using only valid observations, avoiding GRIN's error-propagation and remaining robust under very high missing rates.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The named SPIN baseline in the spatiotemporal-GNN imputation family alongside GRIN; a bidirectional deep SOTA on the air-quality/traffic panels CAFE benchmarks, hence a key 'two-of-three' comparison point (accurate but not point-in-time/CPU-light).

papers.title: Large Dimensional Latent Factor Modeling with Missing Observations and Applications to Causal Inference
papers.methods: Xiong & Pelger estimate a latent factor model from partially observed large panels via PCA on an adjusted covariance matrix, with asymptotic theory for imputed values and a counterfactual/causal-inference application.
papers.relation_to_cafe: The factor-imputation engine underlying Bryzgalova/Pelger's financial imputation; a low-rank panel-completion method that is a parameter regime CAFE claims to generalize (alongside MC-NNM/SoftImpute). Foundational econometrics rival on the factor axis.

threads.paper_title: CSDI: Conditional Score-based Diffusion Models for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation

comments.critique: Reviewer yacf: methodological contribution is limited; the modified denoising function is a straightforward, minimal extension of DDPM.

Reviewer yacf: the importance of the attention mechanism is unclear without comparison; asked for an ablation pitting the proposed attention against Bi-RNN, dilated convolution and flatten/no-temporal/no-feature variants.
Reviewer 2d7W: missing comparisons to standard probabilistic baselines (Multi-task Gaussian Processes, Latent/Neural ODE, mTANs).
Reviewer 2d7W: why was negative log-likelihood (NLL) omitted when evaluating probabilistic interpolation? Requested NLL as an evaluation metric.
Reviewer 2d7W: lacks ablation isolating the contribution of the temporal vs feature transformer layers.
Reviewer 2d7W: discretizing irregularly-sampled data risks information loss.

Reviewer 8rwP: lacks significant novelty; essentially an application of two existing methods (score matching + self-supervised masking already used in audio/NLP/CV inpainting); missing reference to prior inpainting work.
Reviewer 8rwP: move DDPM definition and padding/masking details from appendix into the main text for clarity.
All three reviewers scored 6/10 ('lack of enthusiasm'); PCs accepted anyway citing the important problem and 40-65% empirical gains.

threads.paper_title: Filling the G_ap_s: Multivariate Time Series Imputation by Graph Neural Networks (GRIN)

comments.critique: Reviewer 9yUs: combining time series and graphs is not new; RNN+graph architectures already exist, so novelty is limited.

Reviewer 9yUs and public commenter (Lijun Sun): missing comparisons to low-rank matrix-factorization / low-rank tensor methods (with spatial/temporal regularization) and kriging/graph-signal interpolation baselines (Transdim framework).
Reviewer 9yUs: adding message passing in the recurrent gates adds overhead; provide memory/runtime comparisons to baselines (no empirical cost evidence given).
Reviewer 9yUs: unclear why explicit imputation is needed vs. just running a forecasting model; clarify the imputation-vs-downstream-prediction relationship.
Reviewer jZvK: missing-data simulation is too simple (only 5% block + 25% point missing); test higher missing rates and more patterns, and compare more extensively with BRITS.
Reviewer jZvK and ajb9: static adjacency-matrix assumption is unsuitable for dynamic relational data; address dynamic-graph capability. Also RNN core cannot handle irregularly-sampled data.
Reviewer JPtB: insufficient baselines; add NAOMI, E2GAN, kNN, graph-aware matrix factorization, kriging, and other graph-RNN architectures.

Reviewer hJvE: insufficient theoretical justification for why the graph representation should yield better performance; add motivation for the inductive bias and ablations (fully-connected vs identity adjacency).
Reviewer hJvE: clarify applicability beyond sensor networks (e.g., financial, healthcare panels).

threads.paper_title: Learning to Reconstruct Missing Data from Spatiotemporal Graphs with Sparse Observations (SPIN)

comments.critique: Reviewer 5BtN: requested ablation removing the skip-connection module, and moving ablations into the main text to show component importance.
Reviewer 5BtN and AC: discuss how the imputation method helps other time-series tasks like forecasting; connection to forecasting/other tasks is missing.
Reviewer fr5V: questioned the evaluation methodology, preferring ground-truth reconstruction error over an autoregressive proxy that may be misleading; felt author responses were too brief.
Reviewer fr5V & ajb9: insufficient explanation of sensor-level covariates and the d-dimensional measurement notation; Section 3 / hierarchical attention is too compact to follow.
Reviewer ajb9: the claim that 'GRIN suffers from error propagation typical of autoregressive models' is unjustified and needs a supporting reference.
Reviewer ajb9: static-graph assumption not addressed; graph built from pairwise distances is oversimplified (ignores e.g. sensor elevation).
Reviewer ajb9 & seag & AC: experiments confined to sensor networks (PEMS-BAY etc.); need test cases beyond sensor networks and a clearer practical motivation.

Reviewer seag (1/10) and AC meta-review: novelty is really limited — 'one more way to learn spatio-temporal dependencies via attention'; a GNN over (node, timestep) pairs with attention has been explored before.

threads.paper_title: TimesNet: Temporal 2D-Variation Modeling for General Time Series Analysis

comments.critique: Reviewer v92e: how carefully must the period-count parameter k be chosen, and does larger k help or hurt? Sensitivity unclear.

Reviewer Re8p & gBbZ: the periodicity assumption is problematic for non-strictly-periodic data; the 'general time series' claim may really only hold for periodic series — risks being positioned to a narrower scenario.
Reviewer Re8p: applicability unclear for multi-dataset settings with variable period lengths (e.g., patient hospital data).
Reviewer gBbZ: lacks an ablation on the efficacy of the adaptive aggregation; unclear whether frequency analysis is per-instance or per-batch.
Reviewer gBbZ: the FFT truncate operation is unconvincing as it could blindly discard useful information.
Reviewer gBbZ: DLinear baseline numbers are inconsistent with its original paper and need elaboration.
Reviewer gBbZ: incorporating trend/seasonality component information 'is not a new idea'; technical novelty rated 2/5.
Reviewer v92e & public comment: ethics concern about a near-identical arXiv preprint with author names visible (possible double-blind violation).

threads.paper_title: TSI-Bench: Benchmarking Time Series Imputation

comments.critique: Reviewer Evcs: 'Nothing novel is provided. All the methods and datasets are from existing works'; findings (missing patterns matter, forecasting architectures work for imputation, imputation helps downstream) are unsurprising; better as a journal review.
Reviewers mYVZ & uzuS: missing recent probabilistic/generative imputers (TimeCIB, GRIN, DSPD-GP, TIDER, BiTGraph, mTANs); models considered are outdated.
Reviewer mYVZ: adapting forecasting methods to imputation by merely swapping the output layer is 'unnatural' and doesn't reflect their core purpose.
Reviewer mYVZ: should evaluate downstream models with AND without imputation across multiple model types, not just XGBoost.
Reviewer mYVZ: lacks diverse missing-data scenarios (MNAR vs MCAR, periodic missingness) and deeper analysis of WHY methods excel in given situations; 'experimental design lacks depth'.
Reviewer uzuS: authors don't provide per-method hyperparameters/settings (GP kernels, diffusion noise schedules, timestep configs); unclear if modern methods were tuned optimally on new datasets.
Reviewer uzuS: BRITS outperforms modern methods — is this due to suboptimal tuning of the newer models? Needs explanation.
Reviewer cU7Z: benchmark gives no support for static info (spatial coordinates, descriptive attributes).

Reviewer cU7Z: platform not user-friendly — no documentation, hard-coded missing rates and algorithm list, no clear input/output spec, hard to add new datasets; only good for replicating existing experiments.
Reviewer cU7Z: submission not fully anonymized — an author name appears in supplementary material.

threads.paper_title: Diffusion-based Time Series Imputation and Forecasting with Structured State Space Models (SSSD)

comments.critique: Reviewer 5Tb4: the combination of DiffWave and S4 is 'slightly incremental'.

Reviewer 5Tb4: baseline selection lacks motivation; strong baselines (Autoformer, NAOMI, NRTSI, SAITS) appear inconsistently across experiments — apply the strongest baselines consistently everywhere.
Reviewer 5Tb4: missingness terminology is confusing; clarify how RM/MNR/BM/TF map to the standard MCAR/MAR/MNAR taxonomy.
Reviewer 5Tb4: visualizations show random samples rather than distribution means, and large error bars in Table 4 raise robustness questions.
Reviewer kCUh: S4-layer ablations limited to a single dataset/scenario; provide ablations across RM, MNR and BM at multiple missingness ratios.
Reviewer kCUh: lacks cross-missingness generalization tests (e.g., train at 20% RM, test at 30%; train/inference condition mismatch).
Reviewer kCUh: quantify the diffusion-timestep inference-speed vs accuracy tradeoff; channel-splitting for 100+ channels is unexplained.

Reviewer vTws: concern about data-leakage risk from backward/forward smoothing imputation steps — discuss when backward smoothing introduces future information leakage. (Authors later acknowledged and corrected a Solar-dataset preprocessing leakage, revising test MSE.)

Reviewer vTws & kCUh: insufficient implementation detail — loss function, batching, architecture, and whether all models support backward imputation are not clearly described; missing state-space-hybrid references (Kalman VAE, Deep Kalman Filters).

threads.paper_title: CSDI: Conditional Score-based Diffusion Models for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation

comments.critique: Methodological contribution is rather limited: the method is only a minimal modification of an existing DDPM; the technique combination is described as 'too incremental' and 'essentially applies existing methods without substantial innovation.'

The importance of the two-dimensional (temporal + feature) attention mechanism is unclear without an ablation; reviewers asked for ablations isolating the attention design against alternatives (RNNs, dilated convolutions).
Missing comparisons against relevant probabilistic / continuous-time baselines: Gaussian processes, Neural ODEs, and mTANs.
Missing probabilistic evaluation: reviewer wanted negative log-likelihood (NLL) metrics reported, not just point/CRPS-style metrics.

threads.paper_title: Diffusion-based Time Series Imputation and Forecasting with Structured State Space Models (SSSD)

comments.critique: A data-leakage flaw was identified post-submission: train/test leakage in the Solar dataset preprocessing inflated results; authors had to retrain (MSE worsened from ~2.7e2 to ~5.03e2) and fix the public preprocessing code. (Raised by an external reader, conceded by authors.)

Reviewer asked whether using a backward/smoothing imputation step leaks future information into imputed data when imputation is a precursor to training downstream models, and in which applications a backward step is even justified.

Model and training under-specified: reviewers could not concretely understand how state-space components are used, what loss/batching procedure was used, or how imputation is performed at run-time; requested all architectural components laid out in equation form.

Missingness nomenclature is non-standard and conflated with the literature: what the paper calls RM/MNR/BM/TF should be mapped to MCAR/MAR/MNAR; reviewer noted the paper does not actually consider true MNAR (missingness correlated with the unobserved value).

Baseline selection is inconsistent and under-motivated: strong baselines (NAOMI, NRTSI, SAITS, Autoformer) appear only in selected experiments; reviewer expects the strongest baselines to be run in every experiment where they plausibly apply.
Combining two existing models (DiffWave + S4) is 'slightly incremental.'

S4-layer ablation was shown only for one setting (20% BM on PTB-XL); reviewer requested ablations across multiple missingness types (RM, MNR) and ratios. Also requested study of diffusion-step count vs accuracy (inference-speed/accuracy tradeoff) and of train/test missingness-ratio mismatch generalization.
All models should be evaluated on a common, consistent set of benchmarks for fair cross-experiment comparison.

threads.paper_title: DiffImp: Efficient Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation with Bidirectional Mamba Backbone

comments.critique: Contribution is limited: the work reads as a combination of diffusion + Mamba; the bidirectional-SSM trick is not new (analogous to bi-LSTM), and no theoretical result supports the proposed techniques.

The central claim is linear time complexity, yet runtime/time-cost is essentially absent from the experiments; reviewers found it 'unbelievable' that wall-clock time was omitted given the efficiency claim, and asked for training memory and parameter counts too.

Beating only other diffusion baselines is insufficient; reviewers demanded comparison to broader imputation methods (GNN-based GRIN, GATGPT, sparse spatiotemporal reconstruction) and standard benchmark datasets (PhysioNet 2012 healthcare, air quality).

Only two datasets (Electricity, MuJoCo) used for imputation; the ECG experiment central to SSSD was omitted despite replicating SSSD's other experiments. Reviewers also asked why missing rates differed by dataset (70/80/90% MuJoCo vs 10/30/50% Electricity) instead of a consistent grid, and why baselines weren't run on all datasets.
Only synthetic (injected) missingness is tested; reviewers asked for real-world incomplete datasets to demonstrate effectiveness.

The motivation for modeling inter-channel dependence and for 'backbone compatibility' in diffusion is not established; it reads as an exploratory architecture search without a clear technical/theoretical research question, and the imputation+forecasting scope feels pieced together.

The masking/training strategy and the conditioning signal are not clearly explained: how masks are constructed when data already has/has-no missing values, and how exactly the conditional diffusion conditions are formed and used.

threads.paper_title: LSCD: Lomb-Scargle Conditioned Diffusion for Time Series Imputation

comments.critique: Novelty is limited: the framework is still mainly CSDI with small changes, and using spectral/periodogram information for time series is well-studied; no theoretical analysis of how the Lomb-Scargle periodogram affects the diffusion process.
Empirical gains over the non-spectral diffusion baseline (CSDI) are not significant in the main results table; the spectral component's benefit is not clearly demonstrated.
Lomb-Scargle is more expensive than FFT; reviewers required an analysis of training and inference time / computational efficiency vs FFT, which was missing.

Methodological correctness concern: the spectral consistency loss computes the 'ground-truth' spectrum from the masked observed condition rather than the original full series, and the figure's 'noisy imputation target' appears shifted rather than noise-distorted as in CSDI, suggesting a possible diffusion-process implementation error.

Experimental design unconvincing: synthetic sine data unfairly favors a sinusoidal-assumption method, and real-world irregular series often lack the seasonal structure the method exploits; reviewer questioned whether irregular-series imputation (esp. on medical Physionet data, where missingness is informative of sampling schedule) is even well-motivated.
Code was not actually available at the provided anonymous link; low-resolution figure math; missing related work on irregularly-sampled time series for regression/imputation/forecasting tasks.

threads.paper_title: HDDI: A Historical Data-Based Diffusion Imputation Method for High Missing Rate and Long-Term Gap Multivariate Time Series

comments.critique: Reviewer inspected the code and found the backbone (diff_HDDI) is exactly the CSDI denoiser, which is not disclosed; the only real contribution is a historical-data supplement module, judged insufficient. Incorporating historical data is also a long-standard time-series technique.

Fairness/reproducibility concerns: unclear whether baseline hyperparameters were tuned; baselines absent from the repo so unclear if official code or a unified library (PyPOTS, Time-Series-Library) was used; only one dataset-processing script provided; environment/package versions not listed; standard deviations over the 5 trials omitted.

The sliding-window (step size 1) historical matching scales poorly / linearly with data size; reviewers repeatedly demanded a complexity analysis, window-length selection rationale, and real-time feasibility / production-scaling discussion that the paper lacked.

Baseline set is outdated (mostly pre-2021, only five methods) and omits strong recent imputers; reviewers asked for TimesNet, iTransformer, and notably PriSTI (CSDI+GNN) and GRIN given the long-gap / failed-node setting the paper targets.

Core result tables and even symbol definitions are relegated to the appendix while the main text is sparse on experiments; reviewers cited the ICLR guideline that key evidence must be in the main body; results shown only in normalized form, obscuring real-world benefit.

threads.paper_title: Self-attention-based Diffusion Model for Time-series Imputation in Partial Blackout Scenarios (SADI)

comments.critique: The link between the emphasized 'partial blackout' missingness concept and the actual method is unclear: partial blackout is discussed at length in intro/abstract but barely in the methodology section; reviewers were unconvinced how the architecture is essentially connected to that missing pattern or what advantage it gives over methods that already handle general missing positions.

Claim of modeling feature and temporal dependency 'jointly' is not justified: like CSDI, the model applies feature and temporal blocks sequentially, so reviewers did not accept the 'joint' framing; novelty over existing diffusion imputers not clearly discussed.

Decision-level concern that the main weaknesses were not resolved in rebuttal: drastic performance deterioration in the ablation setting, and the absence of training under the partial-blackout regime itself.

Insufficient interpretation/justification of architecture design and the two-stage loss (eq.16); unclear amount of training data for the synthetic experiments; request to test non-Markov synthetic series rather than only the Markov construction.

Traditional Bayesian/latent-variable generative imputation methods are not discussed; the term 'generative model' is used to mean only deep models, ignoring the broader class; the proposed random-masking 'solution' does not clearly match the missing-pattern criticism raised in the introduction.

threads.paper_title: Low Rank Matrix Completion via Robust Alternating Minimization in Nearly Linear Time

comments.theme: weak baselines / state of the art
comments.critique: The headline running-time result must be judged against the recent Kelner et al. (2023) algorithm, which achieves the same O(|Omega|k) time but with significantly lower sample complexity (no dependence on the condition number kappa). Reviewer asks the authors to justify the significance of their result given a competing method dominates on sample complexity.
The result is purely theoretical and no experiments are provided to demonstrate that the claimed efficiency improvement actually materializes in practice.

Without any discussion of computational limitations or runtime/sample-complexity lower bounds, it is hard to judge whether the near-linear-in-verification-time result is actually significant; the paper should state what runtime one should be aiming for.

Reviewer is unsure of key steps in the forward-error and matrix-perturbation proofs (e.g., why a Pythagorean identity holds, full-column-rank assumptions, a sigma_min bound), flagging confusing/undefined notation and recommending borderline reject pending clarification.
Paper spends too much space on intuition and too little on technical detail in the main body; main theorem appears too late, making the paper dry and hard to verify without reading the appendix.

Reviewer questions whether the per-iteration sample partitioning (sample splitting) can be avoided and asks the authors to clarify whether reusing all samples across iterations breaks correctness or merely complicates the proof.

threads.paper_title: Multi-Mode Deep Matrix and Tensor Factorization

comments.critique: The tensors used in the experiments are quite small; reviewer asks how the proposed model scales to large tensors and notes that running time of the method and baselines is not reported.
Recent nonlinear tensor-completion models (e.g., CoSTCo) are not discussed or compared; more recent methods should be added as baselines.
The proposed models do not consistently outperform existing solutions on the matrix/tensor completion tasks, weakening the empirical case.
Method is evaluated only on matrix and tensor completion, raising doubts about usefulness on other downstream tasks; reviewer wants analysis of the recovered latent factors.

Reviewer questions the realism of the generative assumption X = U^T Q V and asks for real-world motivating examples; another reviewer asks that synthetic data be generated under the exact model assumption (matching activation) to verify recovery.
Computational complexity analysis of the proposed models is not done carefully/elegantly; optimization procedure is not very clearly described.

threads.paper_title: TIDER: Multivariate Time-series Imputation with Disentangled Temporal Representations

comments.critique: The hard-coded decomposition into trend, seasonality, and local/bias factors may not hold across all datasets; some data have no trend or seasonality or contain very unpredictable patterns, and the fixed factors cannot be learned/adapted to unknown or more complex hidden temporal structure.

Biggest concern is that the objective involves many hyperparameters; it is unclear how those choices can be made in practice and how sensitive the results are to them — wrong choices could wipe out the reported gains. Reviewer would reconsider rating if hyperparameter guidance and sensitivity were shown.
The method only slightly outperforms baselines on most datasets; it is hard to say the accuracy differences are statistically significant, making results not fully convincing.

The approach is seen as a fairly simple combination of low-rank matrix factorization with seasonality/trend notions and may not be novel enough for the venue; disentangled factors are pre-defined rather than learned.

Training is fit per individual time series; the latent space is not regularized across the dataset to guarantee generalizable disentanglement, which may limit high-dimensional or strongly cross-correlated settings.

Claim that the method 'scales well to large datasets where deep methods struggle' is misleading — it really concerns scaling to long time series, not large datasets; reviewer also flags redundant repetition in the writing and wants a clearer explanation of how factorization actually imputes missing values.

threads.paper_title: Online Low Rank Matrix Completion

comments.theme: limited novelty / positioning vs prior work
comments.critique: The online low-rank completion setting can be viewed as a contextual low-rank matrix bandit; multiple prior works (Sen 2017, Lu 2018, Jun 2019, Huang 2021, Zhou 2020) are not compared, and the claimed improvement (T^{1/2} vs T^{2/3}) only holds for the rank-1 special case while the general algorithm matches existing rates.
Experiments lack comparison against other recommendation-system / offline algorithms beyond a single UCB baseline.
Code was not provided, so reproducibility is unknown.

Across multiple review rounds the proofs remained 'sloppy' and the manuscript switched back and forth between formulations of the algorithm; a key corollary proof was still incorrect and the resampling procedure's correctness was doubted. Reviewer conditioned a score raise on a clean, self-consistent revision of proofs and appendix.

threads.paper_title: CSDI: Conditional Score-based Diffusion Models for Probabilistic Time Series Imputation
