synthesis.summary: CAFE already does the hard, distinctive work reviewers most respect (mechanical causality verifier, special-case unification, learned-not-tuned dials with per-dial ablation, MCAR/MAR/MNAR+block/subseq patterns, long-gap curves, CRPS/coverage with admitted over-conservatism, 12-seed significance, runtime/scaling, reported-vs-live downstream, registry caveat, HP disclosure). The surviving gaps cluster into five recurring reviewer themes that sank or bruised adjacent papers: (1) baseline breadth and currency—CAFE runs deep bidirectional models but does NOT run the closest CAUSAL/ONLINE statistical rivals it claims to subsume or supersede (SHASTA-PCA, MissNet, online robust tensor, NoTMF, FOCUS, online Gaussian-copula-EM/TGC, dynamic-factor-EM), which is the single most repeated and most acceptance-critical demand across the corpus; (2) the "no-hyperparameter / learned-not-tuned" claim is asserted but never stress-tested—internal constants (semantic harmonic set, g=N/(N+R), nu=4+6/kappa, inverse-variance fusion, window length) are exactly the kind of hidden dials reviewers repeatedly demanded sensitivity curves for, and several papers were dinged precisely for this; (3) scale and dataset diversity (all panels are similar mid-size sensor/macro tables, no high-dimensional or large-N stress, no clinical/healthcare benchmark like PhysioNet, no categorical/mixed-type data); (4) the conservative-interval admission is honest but a fix is now cheap and expected (conformal/quantile wrappers exist and were repeatedly cited as the rigorous answer); (5) theory altitude—CAFE proves point-in-time measurability but offers no consistency/recovery/convergence statement for the estimator itself, a recurring "no theory/identifiability" critique. The highest-leverage, most-tractable single action is to add a causal/online statistical-rival baseline panel; the highest-credibility theory action is a recovery/consistency sketch under the model's own generative assumptions.

ranked_gaps.title: Closest CAUSAL/ONLINE statistical rivals are claimed-subsumed but never run as baselines
ranked_gaps.critique: You run deep bidirectional models (SAITS/BRITS/Transformer/TimesNet/ImputeFormer) and a handful of cheap causal baselines, and you run BayOTIDE — but the methods that occupy your EXACT niche (online + low-rank + robust + factor-AR) are absent from the head-to-head: SHASTA-PCA (streaming heteroscedastic PPCA with missing data), MissNet (KDD'24 CPU SSM + dependency network on the same panels you target — and which you say you 'redesigned away from'), the 2025 online robust tensor recovery (online+robust+anomaly, three of your claims), NoTMF and FOCUS (low-rank dynamic factors + AR, your exact core), and online Gaussian-copula-EM / Temporal Gaussian Copula (TGC). Claiming to 'subsume the mechanics of this cluster' while only racing BayOTIDE invites the reviewer to suspect the omitted rivals would close the gap.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Insufficient/dated baselines is the single most frequent major critique in the corpus and the proximate cause of multiple rejections; here it is sharpened because the missing methods are causal/online (your own ranking lane), so 'they're bidirectional, different game' does not excuse the omission.
ranked_gaps.evidence: Recurs in nearly every thread: TSI-Bench (mYVZ/uzuS 'missing recent methods', BRITS-beats-modern anomaly), GRIN (9yUs/JPtB/Sun: add low-rank MF, kriging, NAOMI, E2GAN, graph-MF), SSSD (5Tb4: apply strongest baselines everywhere), DiffImp (add GRIN/GATGPT), S4M (add GRU-ODE-Bayes/GraFITi/latent-ODE + linear-interp+PatchTST), MambaTS/SAMBA/S7 (must compare against the model you build on), HDDI (add PriSTI/GRIN), Conformal-PID (only ACI baseline). Adjacent papers SHASTA-PCA, MissNet, online-robust-tensor (2511.01267), NoTMF, FOCUS, TGC all exist and are CPU/online.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a 'causal/online statistical rivals' baseline block to the horse race: at minimum SHASTA-PCA, MissNet, the online robust tensor recovery, and NoTMF (online variant), run live on the same 8 panels and masks. Where a method is intrinsically batch (NoTMF, dynamic-factor-EM), run it under your right-edge-readout causal protocol and report the look-ahead Delta exactly as you do for deep models. State explicitly which CAFE by-products each rival lacks.

ranked_gaps.title: The 'no-hyperparameter / learned-not-tuned' claim has no sensitivity evidence for its internal constants
ranked_gaps.critique: You state 'no quantity in the objective is a constant fit to a benchmark,' yet the model carries several fixed internal choices: the semantic harmonic set {7,12,24,48,168,365}, the factor-vs-season gate g=N/(N+R), the kurtosis-to-nu map nu=4+6/kappa, the season-target winsorization (1.5+nu/4)*1.4826, the inverse-variance fusion weight, and the trailing-window length. These ARE hyperparameters by another name. A skeptical reviewer will ask: how sensitive are results to each, and what happens on data whose period is not in your fixed harmonic menu (you already concede aliasing when periods don't match)?
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: 'Zero-config' is a headline selling point; an unsubstantiated no-HP claim is more dangerous than disclosed HPs because reviewers actively probe it. Demonstrating insensitivity converts a soft claim into a hard one; failing to address it lets a reviewer reframe your contribution as 'a model with hidden, untuned constants.'
ranked_gaps.evidence: TIDER (ICLR'23) 'biggest concern is many hyperparameters... unclear how chosen, how sensitive — wrong choices wipe out gains'; Conformal-PID 'many non-intuitive constants C_sat,K_I,eta; appendix shows choices matter enormously'; S4M/TimesNet/FSMamba all asked for systematic sensitivity (k, lambda, K1/K2/tau) across datasets, not one; recurring-demand-synthesis item (5) crisp-novelty/HP transparency.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a one-page sensitivity appendix: tornado/line plots of mean causal MAE vs each internal constant (harmonic-set size, g, the nu map, window length, fusion weight) over the 8 panels, showing the result is flat in a wide band around the chosen value. Add a 'learned periods' robustness check where the harmonic menu is mismatched and quantify the aliasing penalty you already mention, so it is reported rather than discovered.

ranked_gaps.title: Foundation-model imputers ('just use a TSFM') are not engaged
ranked_gaps.theme: missing baselines / positioning vs current SOTA
ranked_gaps.critique: The zero-config / no-per-dataset-tuning pitch now has a direct rival class: time-indexed foundation models that claim zero-shot imputation with no retraining (TabPFN-TS, MoTM, MOMENT, and the 2511.05980 33-dataset study). A reviewer in 2026 will ask why a practitioner would not just run a pretrained TSFM that also needs no tuning, and whether those models — run causally — beat CAFE.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Leaving the most fashionable competing paradigm uncited reads as either unawareness or avoidance; it is the obvious 'have you compared to X' that an AC will forward. Pre-empting it cheaply protects the zero-config claim.
ranked_gaps.evidence: Adjacent papers 2511.05980 (Are TSFMs the future of imputation?), MoTM (2507.13207), MOMENT (ICML'24), ImputeINR/MoTM continuous-modeling thread; corpus repeatedly demands newest baselines (SAMBA/MambaTS: LLM4TS, AutoTimes, GPT4TS; TSI-Bench: outdated models).
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a related-work paragraph distinguishing CAFE from imputation TSFMs (no pretraining corpus, no GPU, strictly causal, per-cell uncertainty + by-products) AND, if feasible, run MOMENT or a TabPFN-TS imputer under your causal right-edge protocol on 2-3 panels to show the look-ahead Delta and the compute gap. Even a cited zero-shot number on Beijing defuses the objection.

ranked_gaps.title: All datasets are similar mid-size panels; no high-dimensional / large-N or healthcare scale stress
ranked_gaps.critique: The eight structured panels are all roughly comparable mid-size sensor/macro/energy tables (~10^2 columns, ~10^4 rows). There is no genuinely high-dimensional panel (1000s of channels), no large-N scale test, and no standard clinical benchmark (PhysioNet 2012) that this community treats as mandatory. Your sub-linear-in-N scaling claim is asserted on the same small panels.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Scale/diversity is the second-most-recurrent demand; benchmark reviewers specifically reject when conclusions rest on few/similar datasets, and a sub-linear-scaling claim invites a request to demonstrate it at scale you have not tested.
ranked_gaps.evidence: ProbTS (M4/M5/FRED/Monash demanded; 'do conclusions hold at larger scale?'); FSMamba (reviewers demanded high-channel data → authors added M5 3049ch, S&P500 1475ch); SPIN/GRIN ('beyond sensor networks'); DiffImp/HDDI/DiffPuter (Covertype 200k, larger datasets); MambaTS ('few datasets, hard to judge significance'). PhysioNet/AQI/ECG named as the standard imputation set in DiffImp/CSDI/SSSD threads.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add (a) one high-dimensional panel (>=1000 channels, e.g. an equity cross-section or M5) to exercise the N-scaling curve at a decade more width, and (b) PhysioNet-2012 (or a clinical EHR panel) under your causal protocol so the healthcare community can locate you. Report the N-scaling slope measured on the wide panel, not just the narrow ones.

ranked_gaps.title: Conservative intervals are admitted but a now-standard calibration fix (conformal/quantile) is neither applied nor benchmarked against
ranked_gaps.critique: You honestly report over-coverage (+0.09 mean excess; Beijing 50%→94%) and defer sharpening to future work. But the field now has cheap, distribution-free wrappers that fix exactly this — split-conformal with missing values, conformalized matrix completion, mask-conditional/weighted conformal, and quantile sub-ensembles. A reviewer will ask why you did not simply wrap CAFE to get calibrated bands, and how your conservative PICP compares to a conformal baseline's guaranteed coverage.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Calibration is repeatedly demanded as a first-class metric, and 'we admit it's wide' is weaker than 'we admit it and show a one-line recalibration recovers nominal coverage.' The fix is causally compatible (a trailing-window conformal layer is point-in-time) and would turn a conceded weakness into a strength.
ranked_gaps.evidence: Conformal-with-missing-values (ICML'23), Conformalized Matrix Completion (NeurIPS'23), Weighted/mask-conditional conformal (2512.14221), Quantile Sub-Ensembles, CopulaCPTS/CoREL/Conformal-PID threads all center coverage+sharpness; CSDI reviewers demanded NLL; recurring 'superiority not established on coverage/width' (CoREL, CopulaCPTS).
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a causal split-conformal (trailing-window) recalibration layer over CAFE's per-cell sigma and report PICP/sharpness before vs after, plus a conformalized-matrix-completion baseline for distribution-free coverage. Show the recalibrated bands hit nominal while staying point-in-time. This is a sigma-only change, so imputation MAE is untouched.

ranked_gaps.title: No recovery/consistency/convergence theory for the estimator itself (only point-in-time measurability)
ranked_gaps.critique: Proposition 1 proves measurability/truncation-invariance — a causality property — but says nothing about whether the alternating-least-squares/EM fit converges, or whether CAFE recovers the true factors/loadings under its own generative model. The adjacent factor-model literature (Bai-Ng, TALL-PROJECT, dynamic-factor-EM, tensor-factor models) routinely supplies consistency and asymptotic normality. A statistics-leaning reviewer will note the gap between your statistical framing and the absence of any estimation guarantee.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: You market CAFE as a principled statistical model, not a heuristic; that framing raises the bar to at least a convergence statement or a recovery sketch. 'No theory' is a recurring major critique, and the comparison class here has theorems.
ranked_gaps.evidence: GRIN/MambaTS/FSMamba/SAMBA/S7 all hit with 'no theoretical justification / proof doesn't make sense / no convergence guarantee'; GINA/not-MIWAE/MissDiff/DiffPuter identifiability-and-convergence demands; adjacent JoE/Biometrika factor papers (2502.04112, 2403.13153, 1910.08273, 2103.03045, 2307.16370) all provide consistency/asymptotic-normality that CAFE lacks.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a short theory paragraph: (a) state the monotone-descent / fixed-point convergence of the IRLS+ALS objective (Eq. obj is biconvex given nu,a), and (b) a recovery sketch — under the generative model (Eq. decomp/dyn) with bounded missingness, the online Kalman+ARD estimate of Wz_t is consistent as the trailing window grows, citing the Bai-Ng / dynamic-factor-EM (2502.04112) results CAFE's regime specializes. Even a clearly-scoped proposition + reference to the parent theorems closes the altitude gap.

ranked_gaps.title: Baseline-tuning fairness for the deep models you run live is not documented
ranked_gaps.critique: You run SAITS/BRITS/Transformer/TimesNet/ImputeFormer yourselves under a causal protocol and report that they 'collapse.' The obvious counter is that they collapse because they were not tuned/trained to convergence for YOUR data and protocol. Without a stated per-deep-model tuning/epoch/HP protocol, a reviewer will argue the right-edge-readout collapse is an artifact of under-training, not an intrinsic property.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Multiple papers were rejected or dinged specifically because baselines underperformed trivial methods and tuning was opaque; since CAFE's headline causal-race result depends on deep models doing badly, the fairness of their setup is load-bearing and will be attacked hardest.
ranked_gaps.evidence: TSI-Bench (uzuS 'BRITS beats modern — suboptimal tuning?'; per-method HPs absent); M3-Impute & MissDiff rejected over baselines worse than mean imputation / opaque tuning; MambaTS AC cited 'fidelity of baseline metrics when not trained to convergence'; SAMBA/MambaTS reviewers re-implemented baselines and got better numbers; DiffPuter/HDDI 'unclear if baselines tuned, official code or unified lib (PyPOTS)'.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a baseline-protocol box: for each deep model state the source (PyPOTS official), epochs/early-stopping, the window length, and that bidirectional numbers reproduce published-range accuracy (proving they ARE adequately trained) so the causal collapse is demonstrably a protocol effect, not under-training. Show each deep model's bidirectional MAE matches its registry value within tolerance.

ranked_gaps.title: No categorical / mixed-type support; numeric-only scope under-stated
ranked_gaps.critique: CAFE is a Gaussian/Student-t factor model over continuous values; categorical and mixed-type features (ubiquitous in real panels and tabular imputation) are not handled or evaluated. The 'just-works 1D/2D/3D library' and structured-panel framing implies broader applicability than a numeric-only model delivers.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Mixed-type handling is a recurrent demand and an explicit rejection reason in the tabular-imputation threads; even if out of scope, an unstated limitation invites a reviewer to overclaim-test it. The online Gaussian-copula rivals you cite handle mixed types, sharpening the contrast.
ranked_gaps.evidence: M3-Impute rejected partly for 'cannot handle categorical features'; not-MIWAE & DiffPuter 'unclear how categoricals evaluated under RMSE / one-hot+mean problematic'; recurring-demand-synthesis item (6) 'handle/evaluate mixed numeric+categorical'; online Gaussian-copula (2009.12326) and TGC explicitly target mixed-type.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add an explicit scope sentence ('CAFE targets continuous panels; categorical/mixed-type imputation is out of scope, served by the copula family') and, ideally, a small bridge: a probit/copula link for binary columns or a demonstration that one-hot columns are handled gracefully. At minimum, state it as a named limitation so it is disclosed rather than discovered.

ranked_gaps.title: Auto-router between joint and per-entity engines is admitted-missing, undercutting 'zero-config'
ranked_gaps.critique: You admit there is no automatic router between the joint and per-entity engines, and that the user must, in effect, know when each applies. That is in tension with the zero-config promise: the practitioner still has to make a structural choice, and the paper's 'which tool when' rule is human-applied, not automated.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Reviewers probe the gap between a 'just-works' claim and residual manual choices; an honest, demonstrated auto-route (or a measured cost of getting it wrong) is far stronger than an admission. You already note the effective-rank readout signals when the factor assumption fails — that is the seed of an automatic switch.
ranked_gaps.evidence: TIDER 'how are choices made in practice'; ProbTS 'no quantifiable rule for which approach suits which dataset'; TimesNet/FSMamba scope-of-claim ('general' may be narrower); your own KNOWN-OPEN list names the missing router.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Either implement a one-line router keyed on the learned effective rank (rank→0 ⇒ switch to per-entity/random-walk prior) and show it recovers the right engine on FX vs structured panels automatically, or add a small table quantifying the MAE cost of choosing the wrong engine so the manual decision's stakes are explicit.

ranked_gaps.title: Irregular / non-uniform sampling not handled, while several rivals make it a feature
ranked_gaps.critique: CAFE operates on a regular time grid (semantic harmonics keyed to fixed periods, AR on z_{t-1}). Irregularly-sampled and event-driven panels — explicitly the domain of BayOTIDE (your nearest causal rival), NCDSSM, mTAN, and the clinical benchmarks — are not addressed. Your own intro motivates 'filings arrive irregularly,' raising the question directly.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Irregular sampling is a recurring critique and a capability your closest cited rival (BayOTIDE) advertises; the mismatch between the motivating sentence and the model's regular-grid assumption is an easy reviewer catch.
ranked_gaps.evidence: CSDI (2d7W: discretizing irregular data loses info; can it handle irregular sampling directly?); LSCD/S4M (irregular-series literature, GRU-ODE-Bayes/GraFITi/CRU missing); BayOTIDE adjacent paper 'handles irregular/arbitrary timestamps'; NCDSSM (ICML'23) targets irregular sampling.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a scope statement that CAFE assumes a regular (or regularized) grid and describe the time-FE/Fourier handling of gaps; optionally demonstrate robustness to mild irregularity by sub-sampling a panel to non-uniform timestamps and reporting the degradation, citing BayOTIDE/NCDSSM as the irregular-native alternatives.

ranked_gaps.title: Cross-missingness / train-test mismatch generalization is not tested
ranked_gaps.critique: You sweep pattern x rate, but you do not show that dials learned under one missingness regime hold up when the deployment regime differs (e.g., learned on 10% point, evaluated on 50% block, or train/inference rate mismatch). For an 'adapts online, no per-dataset tuning' model this is the natural stress test.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Cross-missingness robustness is explicitly demanded in the corpus and is a place where 'learned dials' could silently overfit the seen regime; demonstrating invariance strengthens the adaptivity claim.
ranked_gaps.evidence: SSSD (kCUh: 'train at 20% RM, test at 30%; train/inference condition mismatch'); DiffImp/HDDI inconsistent-grid critiques; M3-Impute 'robustness across missingness types and rates' and 'why better on some datasets'.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a small cross-regime matrix: estimate CAFE under regime A's missingness, evaluate under regime B (rate and pattern mismatched), and show MAE degrades gracefully because the dials are re-estimated online from the actual observed cells. This directly evidences the online-adaptation claim.

ranked_gaps.title: Downstream utility shown only for tree ensembles; no neural/linear downstream and the 'diminishing returns' caveat is unaddressed
ranked_gaps.critique: Your downstream story uses XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost only. Reviewers repeatedly ask for downstream evaluation across model TYPES (with and without imputation, including linear/neural forecasters), and recent work argues better imputation buys little downstream once a model has missingness indicators. The reported-vs-live framing is excellent, but the model-class breadth and the diminishing-returns counterpoint are not engaged.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Downstream-utility scope is a recurring demand, and the 'diminishing returns' result (Le Morvan & Varoquaux, ICLR'25) is a direct threat to any 'imputation improves downstream' claim that a careful reviewer will cite against you.
ranked_gaps.evidence: TSI-Bench (mYVZ: 'multiple model types, not just XGBoost'); M3-Impute/DiffPuter 'no downstream task eval'; adjacent Imputation-for-prediction-diminishing-returns (2407.19804), Task-oriented-via-representers (NeurIPS'24), Chen&McCoy / Bryzgalova finance downstream; GRIN 'why impute vs just forecast'.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add one linear and one neural downstream forecaster to the Online Downstream Test (so it spans tree+linear+neural), and add a paragraph engaging the diminishing-returns result — your live-vs-reported gap is precisely the mechanism that survives it (the gain is causal honesty, not raw reconstruction), which strengthens rather than weakens your case once stated.

ranked_gaps.title: Significance testing is narrow: one rival (causal TRMF), three datasets, one mechanism
ranked_gaps.critique: The 12-seed paired test is rigorous but covers only CAFE vs causal TRMF on three datasets at MCAR(10%). The headline claim is '#1 causal on 7/8 panels' and a flipped leaderboard, yet that ranking carries no error bars or paired significance across the full panel set or against the next-best causal rival (BayOTIDE).
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Reviewers repeatedly note that gains without error bars across enough datasets cannot be judged significant; a leaderboard flip asserted as the central result should itself be significance-tested, not just one auxiliary comparison.
ranked_gaps.evidence: MambaTS/TIDER/M3-Impute ('no error bars / few datasets / hard to judge significance'); CoREL/Copula ('gains in 3rd-4th decimal, practically meaningful?'); your own seed table is limited to TRMF/3 datasets.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the paired multi-seed test to all 8 structured panels and to CAFE-vs-BayOTIDE (the next-best causal method), reporting per-panel CIs and a rank-stability / critical-difference summary so the '#1 causal' and 'leaderboard flips' claims carry significance, not point estimates.

ranked_gaps.title: Anomaly score, dependency network, factors and forecasts are advertised but never quantitatively validated
ranked_gaps.critique: You headline 'one pass yields imputation, forecasting, uncertainty, factors, a streaming anomaly score, a decomposition, and a dependency network,' but only imputation and uncertainty are benchmarked; the rest are shown as illustrations in the appendix. A reviewer will ask whether the anomaly score actually detects anomalies (AUC vs a detector) and whether the dependency network matches ground-truth structure — especially since MissNet, your retired predecessor, validated its network.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Multi-output is a core selling point and a contrast you draw against single-task rivals; advertising capabilities you do not evaluate invites an overclaiming charge, and at least one named rival (MissNet) does validate the dependency network.
ranked_gaps.evidence: Multi-Mode MF ('analysis of recovered latent factors wanted'); MissNet (KDD'24) validates switching sparse networks; SPIN/Casper center the dependency-network output; MOMENT positions multi-task — reviewers expect each advertised task scored.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add at least one quantitative check per advertised by-product: anomaly-detection AUC on a panel with injected/known anomalies (vs a simple detector), and a dependency-network recovery score on a synthetic panel with known sparse structure (vs MissNet's recovered graph). Even one validated by-product converts 'illustrated' into 'demonstrated.'

ranked_gaps.title: Novelty vs the nearest factor+AR+missing-data predecessors not crisply differentiated
ranked_gaps.critique: CAFE's core (low-rank dynamic factors + AR latent state z_t=a z_{t-1} + missingness) is structurally identical to several recent works — NoTMF, LATC, FOCUS (counterfactual forecasting under AR factor dynamics), and dynamic-factor-EM (2502.04112). Your special-case table lists classic methods but not these direct contemporaries. A reviewer will ask 'how is this different from FOCUS/NoTMF beyond engineering?'
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Crisp novelty differentiation from near-neighbors is a recurring rejection driver; the danger here is acute because the closest works share your two signature ingredients, so the burden is on you to name them and itemize what is genuinely new (learned dials, robustness, causal verifier, per-cell UQ, fixed effects+season, one objective).
ranked_gaps.evidence: CSDI/SSSD/DiffImp/SAMBA/S7/M3-Impute/MissDiff all hit with 'incremental / not differentiated from prior X'; recurring-demand-synthesis item (5) 'differentiate novelty crisply from near-neighbour methods'; adjacent FOCUS (2511.06189, 'same two ingredients'), NoTMF, LATC, dynamic-factor-EM.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a 'closest contemporaries' subsection or extend the special-case table to FOCUS/NoTMF/LATC/dynamic-factor-EM with an explicit per-feature checklist (causal-verified / learned-not-tuned / Student-t / fixed effects+season / per-cell UQ / online) showing which each lacks. This pre-empts the 'just another factor+AR model' framing.

ranked_gaps.title: MNAR is admitted-unmodelled, but an available identification lever (MNAR matrix completion) is not adopted or benchmarked
ranked_gaps.critique: Your MNAR scope note is honest and well-cited (Ma&Zhang, causal-view recoverability), and you report bounded degradation with the censoring bias. But the panel-MNAR literature now offers concrete recoverability machinery (Bhattacharya/Athey-style MNAR matrix completion, DMM nonlinear-ICA identifiability, not-MIWAE) that you could either adopt or benchmark against rather than only cite as a non-identifiability disclaimer.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: MNAR mechanism handling and identifiability is one of the most recurrent demands; 'we make no MNAR model' is defensible but stronger if paired with a comparison to a method that does, quantifying what an explicit MNAR model buys (or doesn't) on your panels.
ranked_gaps.evidence: TSI-Bench/SSSD/DiffImp/DiffPuter/M3-Impute all demand explicit MCAR/MAR/MNAR with stated mechanisms and identifiability discussion; adjacent MNAR-MC-for-causal-panels (2308.02364), DMM (2505.07180), GNR (CIKM'23), GINA/not-MIWAE provide the levers.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a single MNAR baseline that DOES model the mechanism (e.g., the MNAR matrix-completion estimator of 2308.02364 or a not-MIWAE-style fit) to the MNAR-scope table, showing whether explicit MNAR modeling materially beats CAFE's ignorable fit on your self-masking setup — turning the disclaimer into a measured comparison.

ranked_gaps.title: Runtime/scaling compared only to CPU baselines; the ~1000x compute-gap claim vs deep models is asserted, not measured side-by-side
ranked_gaps.critique: You report CAFE's 1.16s and linear-T/sub-linear-N scaling against SoftImpute/TRMF, and assert a ~10^3x compute gap vs GPU deep imputers. But the deep-model side of that ratio is not measured in the same table (training time, memory, parameter counts, per-fill inference cost). Efficiency claims with the expensive side left out are exactly what reviewers flag as 'unbelievable.'
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Efficiency is a headline (CPU-only is one of your two-of-three). Reviewers demanded wall-clock + memory + params whenever an efficiency claim appeared, and rejected when omitted; the 1000x figure needs at least one measured anchor.
ranked_gaps.evidence: DiffImp ('linear-time claim but runtime totally ignored — unbelievable; want memory + params'); S7/MambaTS/LSCD/S4M/M3-Impute ('efficiency claimed, no FLOPs/runtime/memory'); HDDI/DiffPuter (K-fold EM cost must be quantified in main text).
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add measured training+inference wall-clock, peak memory, and parameter count for at least 2 deep imputers (e.g., SAITS, CSDI/ImputeFormer) on one panel next to CAFE's 1.16s/CPU, so the ~1000x gap is a measured row rather than a rhetorical figure. Note CAFE has zero training phase.

ranked_gaps.title: Fairness of the causal protocol: the right-edge-readout handicap on deep models may be argued unfair
ranked_gaps.critique: Your causal horse race runs deep bidirectional models as filters via right-edge readout, where they 'collapse.' A reviewer sympathetic to those models will argue this is an unfair handicap — the architectures were designed bidirectionally, so penalizing them for not being causal is comparing them off-design, and a causal-native deep model (e.g., a unidirectional/filtering variant, or SSSD-as-filter) should be the fair comparison.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: The causal protocol is your central contribution and its fairness will be the most scrutinized methodological choice; conceding and addressing the 'off-design handicap' counterargument pre-empts the strongest rebuttal a deep-model advocate can mount.
ranked_gaps.evidence: SSSD/CSDI leakage threads (backward-smoothing-as-leakage debated, authors conceded a real leak); MambaTS 'baselines not trained to convergence is unfair'; CopulaCPTS 'were calibration-free baselines given the extra data — otherwise unfair'; general fairness-of-protocol scrutiny throughout.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add a causal-native deep baseline (a unidirectional/streaming variant or a deep filter trained causally) to show the collapse is not merely a readout handicap but reflects the information genuinely withheld; and add a sentence framing right-edge readout as the honest deployment use of a bidirectional model, with the causal-native deep model as the fair upper bound.

ranked_gaps.title: Heavy-tail robustness benchmarked only via the ablation, not against dedicated robust low-rank methods
ranked_gaps.critique: The Student-t dial is validated by an ablation (HeavyT 1.16→2.10), but not against the dedicated robust low-rank / heavy-tailed estimators that constitute the alternative answer to the same problem: Huber-loss matrix completion (JASA 2025), T-Rex (Tyler M-estimator factor EM), elliptical-factor methods, robust RRR with missing data. You position against this line in prose but never race it.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: When you make robustness a learned dial and a selling point, the robust-MC community will want to see you beat (or match) their purpose-built estimators on heavy-tailed data, not just beat your own ablated self.
ranked_gaps.evidence: Adjacent Robust-MC-heavy-tailed (2206.04276), T-Rex (2505.12117), tail-robust factor (2407.09390), robust-RRR-missing (2512.24450), RPCA-IRLS (2412.14629); corpus 'apply strongest baselines everywhere' (SSSD).
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: Add one dedicated robust estimator (T-Rex or Huber-MC) as a baseline on the heavy-tailed regime and on a panel with injected outliers, showing CAFE's learned-nu matches or beats it while also being causal/online — converting the robustness claim from internal-ablation to external-comparison.

ranked_gaps.title: Static covariates / side information cannot be incorporated
ranked_gaps.critique: CAFE uses only the value panel; static side information (sensor coordinates, entity attributes, spatial graph) that spatiotemporal rivals exploit cannot be injected. On the sensor/traffic panels you use, competitors gain from exactly this signal, so a like-for-like comparison may understate or overstate depending on whether rivals used it.
ranked_gaps.why_it_matters: Static-covariate support is a named reviewer concern and a real capability gap vs graph-based rivals on the spatial datasets in your suite; disclosing it clarifies the comparison and forestalls 'unfair to graph methods' or 'misses available signal.'
ranked_gaps.evidence: TSI-Bench (cU7Z: 'no support for static info — spatial coordinates, attributes'); SPIN/GRIN/Casper/ImputeFormer all use spatial graphs/coordinates CAFE ignores.
ranked_gaps.recommended_action: State the limitation explicitly and, optionally, show that the learned dependency network recovers the spatial adjacency that graph methods are given a priori — turning the missing-input into evidence that CAFE infers the structure rather than needing it supplied.

also_consider: Reproducibility/anonymization scrub before submission: multiple adjacent papers (TSI-Bench global_config.py author leak, TimesNet arXiv-preprint deanonymization, LSCD dead code link) were dinged or risked desk-reject on anonymity/code-availability; CAFE already has HP disclosure but should ensure the cafe library, bench scripts, and any author byline (the README author byline in recent commits) are scrubbed/anonymized for double-blind and that bench/make_paper.py runs from a clean checkout.

Presentation/altitude: several papers were criticized for relegating key tables/definitions to the appendix (HDDI, Low-Rank-MC-AltMin); CAFE pushes the by-product outputs and full ablation matrix to the appendix — verify the main-text experimental evidence is self-sufficient under venue page limits.

Hankel/circulant low-rank branch (Hankel Imputation 2408.02594, Laplacian Convolutional Representation TKDE) is a purely-statistical batch alternative CAFE could add as one more 'special-case / supersedes' citation, but it is lower priority than the causal/online rivals and is already partially covered by the special-case framing.

NLL as an uncertainty metric was repeatedly requested in CSDI threads; CAFE deliberately drops NLL (not comparable across families per the hardening notes) and uses CRPS/PICP/sharpness instead — this is a defensible, already-reasoned choice, so it is excluded from the ranked gaps, but a one-line justification in the paper would pre-empt the recurring 'why no NLL' question.

Task-oriented imputation evaluation (generalized representers, NeurIPS'24; TOI-VSF) argues reconstruction error is the wrong objective — CAFE already engages this via the Online Downstream Test and the 'reconstruction != utility' paragraph, so it is mostly covered; a citation to the representer line would round it out.

Diminishing-returns and constant-imputation-competitiveness (Le Morvan & Varoquaux ICLR'25; CHIL'25 linear-interp-beats-11-SOTA; Chen&McCoy finance) partly support CAFE's own narrative and are partly cited (Bryzgalova) — folded into gap #12 rather than listed separately.
